title: Cutting out the Cohen-Macaulay locus for a groupoid with flat finitely presented structure maps, yielding a Cohen-Macaulay restriction with surjective structure maps

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-make-CM (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 840-860

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Apply the local-source lemma with g = id, Q = locally of finite presentation, R = flat and locally of finite presentation, P = Cohen-Macaulay, via the local-source-apply remark: this gives an open U' of U with t^{-1}(U') the largest open subscheme of R on which s is Cohen-Macaulay, proving (1). Let i be the inverse of the groupoid; since i is an isomorphism with s composed with i = t and t composed with i = s, the open s^{-1}(U') is likewise the largest open on which t is Cohen-Macaulay, proving (2). By the flat-finite-presentation-CM-open lemma the CM-locus open is dense in every fibre of the flat finitely presented structure map; since the structure maps have the identity section, density in every fibre gives nonempty intersection, i.e. surjectivity, proving (3) and symmetrically (4). Part (5) is a formal consequence of (1), (2) and the restriction discussion of the groupoids chapter: on R' = s^{-1}(U') intersect t^{-1}(U') the restriction (U', R', s', t', c') is a groupoid whose source and target are Cohen-Macaulay (each lies in the respective largest CM-open) and locally of finite presentation (restrictions of locally finite presentation morphisms). (source lines 862-887)

core_obligations: Apply lemma-local-source with g = id and Q = locally of finite presentation, R = flat and locally of finite presentation, P = Cohen-Macaulay, via remark-local-source-apply: this yields an open U' of U with t^{-1}(U') the largest open subscheme of R on which s is Cohen-Macaulay, proving (1) (proof lines 862-874). Symmetrize with the inverse: i : R to R is an isomorphism with s composed with i = t and t composed with i = s, so s^{-1}(U') is the largest open on which t is Cohen-Macaulay, proving (2) (proof lines 875-878). Surjectivity: by more-morphisms-lemma-flat-finite-presentation-CM-open the CM-locus open is dense in every fibre of the flat finitely presented structure map; the identity section e makes every fibre nonempty, so the dense intersection is nonempty, giving a point over every u in U; this proves (3) and the same argument with the roles of s and t swapped proves (4) (proof lines 879-883). Part (5): R' = s^{-1}(U') intersect t^{-1}(U') with the restricted structure maps is a groupoid by the restriction discussion of the groupoids chapter; s' is Cohen-Macaulay because R' sits inside the largest s-CM-open t^{-1}(U'), t' because R' sits inside s^{-1}(U'), and both are locally of finite presentation as restrictions of s, t; a formal consequence of (1), (2) and the restriction machinery (proof lines 884-886).
proof_roadmap: Instantiate the local-source lemma with P = Cohen-Macaulay, Q = lfp, R = flat lfp, g = id to get the largest s-CM-open over U' (proof lines 862-874).
Use the groupoid inverse to symmetrize the maximality for t (proof lines 875-878).
Derive surjectivity (3), (4) from fibre density of the CM-locus opens plus the identity section (proof lines 879-883).
Assemble the restricted groupoid R' on U' with Cohen-Macaulay, finitely presented structure maps from (1), (2) and the restriction discussion (proof lines 884-886).
